Title: Diagnosis

Details: The failing test `testReflectionObjectCycle` creates two objects referencing each other, which previously caused a `StackOverflowError` due to infinite recursion in the reflection-based hash code computation. The code under test is the `HashCodeBuilder.reflectionHashCode` method that ultimately calls `reflectionAppend`. This method invokes itself recursively up the class hierarchy to build a hash code reflectively by accessing fields. To avoid infinite recursion on cyclic object graphs, `reflectionAppend` uses a registry (`REGISTRY`), a `ThreadLocal` holding a `Set` of `IDKey` objects that wrap visited objects. The methods `isRegistered`, `register`, and `unregister` respectively check presence, add, and remove an object in this registry. The test asserts after hashCode computation that the registry is cleared (`assertNull(HashCodeBuilder.getRegistry())`), verifying no ThreadLocal state leak.

The current bug report highlights that the `ThreadLocal` used in `ToStringStyle` and `HashCodeBuilder` is never properly removed, causing memory leaks in container environments such as servlet containers where classes may be reloaded across applications.

Although the `reflectionAppend` method uses `register` and `unregister` calls in a `try`/`finally` block, the registry is implemented as a ThreadLocal set that is never cleared from the thread after use, with no public API to remove it. This may lead to the observed memory leak since the ThreadLocal will retain references to objects or classes indefinitely.

Hence, the bug occurs because while the recursion cycle is prevented correctly by maintaining a ThreadLocal registry of visited objects, this registry is never fully cleared from the ThreadLocal after the top-level hash code computation completes, leading to potential memory leaks when threads live a long time and repeatedly use HashCodeBuilder in container environments.

The test failure signals the behavior of using the registry, but the main issue from the current bug report is the missing cleanup of the ThreadLocal itself, leading to leaks.

Recent bug reports do not provide any direct relevance to the ThreadLocal usage in builders here.

Thus, the root cause is the incomplete lifecycle management of the ThreadLocal registry in `HashCodeBuilder` class: it should provide means to clear the registry from ThreadLocal or remove it after computation, but it currently does not.

Based on the code snippets, the faulty logic centers around:

- `HashCodeBuilder.REGISTRY` (the ThreadLocal itself), which never removes the ThreadLocal set
- `HashCodeBuilder.getRegistry()` returning the ThreadLocal value without clearing it
- `HashCodeBuilder.reflectionCappend` managing recursion but not clearing the ThreadLocal on top-level calls

Fixes should address proper removal of the entry in ThreadLocal after hash code computation to prevent memory leaks.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
